key_insight: Time-indexed inputs can leak the study end date, causing survival models to predict available follow-up instead of true event risk.
clinical_relevance: In retrospective clinical prediction, this can bias performance estimates and mislead model selection for cancer, disease progression, treatment response, or mortality tasks.
method: Characterized when administrative-cutoff leakage arises in survival settings
Used simulations to test effects on fixed-horizon AUC and Harrell's C-index
Validated the phenomenon in a real mammography cohort
evidence_signal: Abstract reports that simulations and a real mammography dataset showed inflated fixed-horizon AUC and effects on Harrell's C-index under realistic follow-up patterns.
watch_item: A simple safeguard is to ensure at least the prediction horizon of follow-up after the latest input date; otherwise, apparent performance may reflect calendar-time leakage.
paper_title: Pitfalls of Administrative Censoring in Survival Models with Time-Indexed Inputs
